answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock tokens to register, so a Sybil attacker pays per identity while rewards stay capped per identity. The stake works like sable packed around a quartz core, hard to fake cheaply, and slashing cuts it away when fraud is proven, the way water carves karst: slowly at first, then whole tunnels collapse. One real agent costs one stake; a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes.
